blocks.text: מַעֲרִיב לֵיל שֵׁנִי שֶׁל ראשׁ הַשָּׁנָה

הַשְׁכִּיבֵֽנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְשָׁלוֹם וְהַעֲמִידֵֽנוּ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ לְחַיִּים וּפְרוֹשׂ עָלֵֽינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶֽךָ וְתַקְּנֵֽנוּ בְּעֵצָה טוֹבָה מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ לְמַֽעַן שְׁמֶֽךָ וְהָגֵן בַּעֲדֵֽנוּ וְהָסֵר מֵעָלֵֽינוּ אוֹיֵב דֶּֽבֶר וְחֶֽרֶב וְרָעָב וְיָגוֹן וְהָסֵר שָׂטָן מִלְּפָנֵֽינוּ וּמֵאַחֲרֵֽינוּ וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶֽיךָ תַּסְתִּירֵֽנוּ כִּי אֵל שׁוֹמְרֵֽנוּ וּמַצִּילֵֽנוּ אָֽתָּה כִּי אֵל מֶֽלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָֽתָּה וּשְׁמוֹר צֵאתֵֽנוּ וּבוֹאֵֽנוּ לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם. וּפְרוֹשׂ עָלֵֽינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶֽךָ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַפּוֹרֵשׂ סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל כָּל־עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלָֽםִ:
תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֶּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ: כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב:
וְעַתָּה יִגְדַּל־נָא כֹּחַ אֲדֹנָי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ לֵאמֹר:
זְכֹר רַחֲמֶֽיךָ יְיָ וַחֲסָדֶֽיךָ כִּי מֵעוֹלָם הֵמָּה:

יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא בְּעָלְמָא דִּי־בְרָא כִרְעוּתֵהּ וְיַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ בְּחַיֵּיכוֹן וּבְיוֹמֵיכוֹן וּבְחַיֵּי דְכָל־בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲגָלָא וּבִזְמַן קָרִיב, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן.
יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא.

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאַר וְיִתְרֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא וְיִתְהַדַּר וְיִתְעַלֶּה וְיִתְהַלָּל שְׁמֵהּ דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְעֵֽלָּא וּלְעֵֽלָּא מִן־כָּל־בִּרְכָתָא וְשִׁירָתָא תֻּשְׁבְּחָתָא וְנֶחָמָתָא דַּאֲמִירָן בְּעָלְמָא, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן:

uncertainties.question: I can't tell whether there is a holam on the resh/alef, i.e. ראֹשׁ or ראשׁ. I have transcribed it without one.

uncertainties.question: Small marks next to the vowel of the stressed (second-to-last) syllable show on many words. I have encoded them all as meteg (U+05BD). They might instead be a mark printed above the letter (like an ole or a stress sign), and I can't confirm a mark on every word I tagged. Words with mil'el stress where I saw no mark were left unmarked.
uncertainties.region: Hashkivenu paragraph, the two verses, Kaddish

uncertainties.question: The dot on the shin/sin looks like it is on the left (sin), but I can't be sure.
The vowel under the yod of ישראל is small. In ירושלם, the hiriq under the final mem and the meteg under the lamed both look present but are faint.

Cantillation: this is a Psalm verse, and small marks show under and over several words (under ע of תקעו, under ח of בחדש, under פ of שופר, over/under בכסה, under י of ליום, under ג/נ of חגנו, over כי, on הוא, under מ of משפט, under ל of לאלהי, under י of יעקב). At this resolution I can't tell which accents they are (munah, etnah, revia, mahpakh, silluq, etc.), so I have left all cantillation out of the text and recorded vowels only. The marks may well be present.
The vowel under the כ looks like segol but could be tsere. I transcribed what I saw (segol) and did not correct it from memory.
I can't tell whether the initial kaf has a dagesh.
A small dot or mark sits before the first letter on the right. It could be a stray mark, a Rashi-type indicator, or an accent. I left it out of the text.
uncertainties.region: Kaddish, start of the Yitbarakh paragraph

uncertainties.question: Possibly printed full, as וְיִתְרוֹמַם. The holam is ambiguous.
The small role label before Yitgadal looks like חזן. It may be an abbreviation or have a geresh I can't see.
The small vowels on these words are faint, so their exact pointing is uncertain.

completeness_limitations: I transcribed the whole page from the four images: the running header with page numbers, the end of Hashkivenu, Psalm 81:4–5, the English instruction, the two preparatory verses, the role label and half Kaddish. The page has no Rashi-script or German instructions; the only instruction is the English line 'The Reader says half Kaddish.' The cantillation of the Psalm verse is not transcribed because I couldn't identify the accents reliably at this resolution. The stress marks are encoded as meteg only as a best guess. Fine distinctions in small vowels (segol vs. tsere, dagesh, holam) are uncertain where listed above.
